title: Property wrappers and result builders, from the outside in

videos.script: Some Swift reads strangely the first time. An at sign in front of a property. A dollar sign in front of its name. A block of lines with no commas and no return. {{wrapper}} This lesson takes each one apart, from the outside in. First the property wrapper. A rule about one value, written once, and applied with an at sign. You will write one that keeps a session between zero and six hundred minutes. {{dollar}} Then the dollar sign, which is the wrapper's second face. Ours says whether a value was cut down. {{builder}} Then the result builder. A block where each line becomes part of a value. Swift's own regex builder runs here, and then you write one for the week's report. {{macro}} Last, macros, which are programs the compiler runs on your code. You will print what one of them wrote, line by line. SwiftUI is built from all three. It does not run on Linux, so you build small versions and read the real ones.
